Fill placeholders with R content

replace_placeholders.Rd

Swaps each placeholder (placeholder_prefix followed by an ID) in a Markdown file for the content given in code_content. Code isn't run here. It's written into the Markdown as inline R or a chunk, and runs when Quarto renders the document.

Each piece of content is written with a marker naming its placeholder (see marker_mode) and, in draft mode, wrapped in draft markers:

DRAFT_CONTENT_START
<marker>
<content>
DRAFT_CONTENT_END

Together these let clean_markdown() turn the content back into its placeholder when the document returns from Word, so it can be filled again. vignette("knittogether") explains the round trip.

Usage

replace_placeholders(
  markdown_file,
  placeholder_prefix = "placeholder_",
  code_content = list(),
  draft_mode = TRUE,
  draft_mode_prefix = "DRAFT_CONTENT_START",
  draft_mode_suffix = "DRAFT_CONTENT_END",
  validation_path = NULL,
  marker_mode = c("hidden", "show", "off"),
  placeholder_style_hidden = "PlaceholderMarker",
  placeholder_style_visible = "PlaceholderMarkerVisible",
  log_file = "quality_log.csv",
  html_file = "validation.html",
  output_file_ext = "md",
  output_file = NULL,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

Arguments

markdown_file

Path to the Markdown file to fill.

placeholder_prefix

The text every placeholder starts with, used exactly as given. The placeholder is the prefix followed by the ID, so the default "placeholder_" with the ID plot gives placeholder_plot. Choose any prefix that won't appear by accident in normal writing, such as "knit_" or "xyz_". Use the same prefix in clean_markdown() and replace_placeholders(). Defaults to "placeholder_".

code_content

The content for each placeholder, as made by placeholder_map().

draft_mode

Logical. If TRUE (the default), wrap each piece of content in draft markers. Keep this on while the document is still going back to Word. If FALSE, no draft markers are written, and any draft blocks already in the file are turned back into placeholders and filled, so you can make the final version straight from a draft.

draft_mode_prefix, draft_mode_suffix

The lines that start and end a draft block. Defaults to "DRAFT_CONTENT_START" and "DRAFT_CONTENT_END". Avoid --, which Word turns into a dash.

validation_path

Folder for the validation log, a CSV of which placeholders were found and filled and what changed since the last run. If the quarto and reactable packages are installed, an HTML version is made too. Defaults to NULL, which writes no log.

marker_mode

How the marker naming each placeholder is written:

  • "hidden" (the default) uses the placeholder_style_hidden style, which can be set to hidden text in Word.

  • "show" uses the placeholder_style_visible style.

  • "off" writes no marker. Use this only for the final version: nothing is left to show where the content came from, so it can't be refreshed after another round in Word.

In HTML output, hide_markers_css() hides the markers.

placeholder_style_hidden, placeholder_style_visible

Names of the Word character styles used for markers. Defaults to "PlaceholderMarker" and "PlaceholderMarkerVisible". The package includes a Word document with both styles set up: system.file("extdata", "PlaceholderMarker_example.docx", package = "knittogether").

log_file, html_file

File names for the validation log and its HTML version, inside validation_path. Set either to NULL to skip it. Defaults to "quality_log.csv" and "validation.html".

output_file_ext

Extension for the output file when output_file isn't given. Defaults to "md". Use "qmd" if Quarto complains about executable code in a .md file.

output_file

Path to write the result to, leaving the input file unchanged. Defaults to NULL, which writes to markdown_file (with its extension changed to output_file_ext).

overwrite

Logical. If FALSE, stop rather than write over an existing file. Defaults to TRUE. Use timestamped_path() to keep earlier versions.

Value

The filled Markdown, invisibly, as a character string.

See also

define_content(), placeholder_map(), clean_markdown()

Other workflow: clean_markdown(), convert_markdown(), run_workflow()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plot <- define_content(
  placeholder_id = "plot",
  description = "Car weight against fuel economy",
  output_mode = "chunk",
  content = { plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg) },
  chunk_options = list(echo = FALSE)
)

# While the document is still a draft
replace_placeholders(
  markdown_file = "draft.md",
  placeholder_prefix = "placeholder_",
  code_content = placeholder_map(specs = list(plot)),
  validation_path = "validation"
)

# The final version
replace_placeholders(
  markdown_file = "draft.md",
  placeholder_prefix = "placeholder_",
  code_content = placeholder_map(specs = list(plot)),
  draft_mode = FALSE,
  marker_mode = "off"
)
} # }
